en.title: Disney's Hexed Unleashes a Witchy Mother-Daughter Spell
en.summary: Disney Animation's 65th feature, Hexed, conjures a vibrant world where inanimate objects come alive and magic flows through generations. This enchanting tale centers on a rebellious teen discovering her lineage and the complicated bonds of family.
en.body:
Disney Animation Studios is stepping into a new era of enchantment with **Hexed**, its 65th full-length feature, which conjures a world entirely steeped in magic. This ambitious film transports audiences to the mystical realm of Hexe, a land of eternal autumn where every object, from tumbleweeds to cauldrons, possesses a life of its own. More than just a visual spectacle, **Hexed** casts a sincere story about the intricate relationships between mothers, daughters, and the enduring power of intergenerational parenting.

The heart of the narrative beats with **Billie Doe** (voiced by **Hailee Steinfeld**), a spirited and rebellious teenager who feels like an outsider in her suburban life, amplified by her overprotective mother, **Alice** (voiced by **Rashida Jones**). When an impulsive act leads Billie to a magical charm her mother gave her, a portal opens, whisking her away from Ohio to the bewitching world of Hexe. There, she discovers she hails from a long line of powerful witches, with her formidable grandmother, **Queen Celeste** (voiced by **Jodie Foster**), in pursuit. To navigate this new reality and understand her destiny, Billie must reluctantly team up with her mother and her cantankerous, three-eyed, green-cat familiar, **Beef Roger Crummchuk** (voiced by **Walton Goggins**). Together, they must unravel family secrets and fulfill a magical prophecy that holds the key to their understanding each other.

## A Spellbinding Shift in Storytelling

The journey to **Hexed** involved a significant creative evolution. Initially conceived with a different familial dynamic, the film's directors, **Fawn Veerasunthorn** and **Jason Hand**, along with co-director **Josie Trinidad**, refined the story to focus on the complex mother-daughter bond. Producers **Roy Conli** and **Yvett Merino** have spoken about this crucial shift, emphasizing how exploring intergenerational parenting became the film's strongest spell. This focus allows **Hexed** to delve into the unique challenges and profound love that define these relationships, making the magic of Hexe a backdrop for deeply human connection.

## For the Fans: A New Kind of Disney Magic

For fans of Disney Animation, **Hexed** represents a thrilling departure. The promise of a world where inanimate objects come alive, combined with a narrative centered on relatable family dynamics and the discovery of hidden powers, is a potent mix. The film’s rich fantasy setting and the ensemble voice cast, featuring acclaimed talent like **Hailee Steinfeld**, **Rashida Jones**, **Walton Goggins**, and **Jodie Foster**, are sure to ignite excitement. The anticipation for this unique blend of magic, humor, and heartfelt emotion is palpable, as audiences eagerly await a story that speaks to both the wonder of fantasy and the complexities of family.

## What's Next

**Hexed** is set to premiere at the El Capitan Theatre on November 12, 2026, with a wider theatrical release scheduled for November 25, 2026. Audiences can expect a magical adventure that promises to enchant and resonate long after the credits roll.

content_raw: Walt Disney Animation Studios has created countless magical worlds but not one completely made of magic. So enters the witchy world of Hexe in the animation house’s latest full-length film, Hexed . Marking the legendary studio’s 65th feature, Hexed transports audiences to a fantasy realm full of witches, wizards, and familiars (talking animals) who live in an eternal autumn setting. Within Hexe, every inanimate object comes alive, from tumbleweeds to cauldrons and doors. Yet it’s also the setting where the film casts a sincere story about mothers and daughters and intergenerational parenting, and the curses and magic it spurs.  The film is centered on Billie Doe ( Hailee Steinfeld ), a rebellious, overeager, and spirited teen. She feels outcast by her typical high school life and even more so by her overprotective mother Alice (Rashida Jones). When Billie gets expelled from school and takes off for the first time the charm Alice made for her as a baby, a portal opens up. Transported from her Ohio suburbs to the magical Hexe, Billie quickly learns that she comes from a long lineage of witches. As her powerful grandmother Queen Celeste (Jodie Foster) is on the search for her, Billie must team up with her mom and her disgruntled three-eyed, green-cat familiar Beef Roger Crummchuk (Walton Goggins) to uncover family secrets and fulfill a magical prophecy that hopefully spellbinds them to finally understand each other.  Den of Geek had the chance recently to speak with Hexed producers Roy Conli and Yvett Merino, and directors Jason Hand and Fawn Veerasunthorn about bringing inanimate objects to life, changing the story from being about a mother-son dynamic to a mother-daughter one, and exploring intergenerational parenting as the film’s strongest spell. How did you create language with spells through hand movements? What was that process like? Fawn Veerasunthorn, co-director: With magic in this movie, we relate that to each character’s potential. So they must have that character’s personality showing up in the magic. I love films and books that have their own magic system, so when I hopped on the project, I’m like, “Let’s talk about if I were to go to Hexe. How do I learn to do magic? I just want to be able to do this just like Billie.” And the idea of intention, ignition and inwitchification is speaking to the person knowing what they want. Ignition is a spark inside each of you, which is highly individualized. And then witchification is the action you must take in order to make something happen. So we build it from the ground up like that. Roy Conli, producer: It was interesting, though, because we had a lot of animation tests early on before we actually even landed on ‘the Three Is’ [of Intention, Ignition, and Inwitchification]. And we just asked people, give us ideas. And some were turned in hand-drawn, some were in CG, and from that plethora of information, we just started getting the hands movements
